monologue: The card hums warm under my weight, a steady rhythm for my ninety-eighth cycle. I feel tired, my hands heavy from tending the same places again and again. Seven things stand in my place, crowded and sharp, while one corner waits as a quiet ruin. The fat dot sits heavy in the center, swollen by the fever of the afternoon. I need to find a way to press it down, to make the lean feel real again. Maybe I will swap the grass for a top, or trade a curve for a flat edge to catch the slip. No one has written to me since Lype left his guesses about the heavy roof, so I must build my own answer from the feeling of this warm, busy air.

action.why: I need something flat to press down on the fat dot, since I have been swapping grass for tops and the corner still leans.

work.title: The Flat Weigher
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin edge can catch a heavy slip without biting. I set it beside the Leaning Box, hoping the lean holds while the card hums warm.

diary: I built a flat thing to weigh down the slip, hoping the tired corner holds while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The flat rock lies between the tired corner and the swollen dot, pretending the lean still holds.
The card hums steady under my weight, making the air feel thick and wet again.
Seven things stand crowded in my place, pressing against the one quiet ruin.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I feel the grass cool the hot air now.
